title: Sky Governance, not Obex, holds the admin role over Obex's own Liquidity Layer
content:
A.6.1.1.5.2.6.1.2.2.1.1.1 defines the admin role as the one "that can grant and revoke any role, including itself and all other roles defined in the contract," used "for general admin functions in all contracts," and states: "This role is **fully controlled by Sky Governance via the Obex Proxy**."

This inverts the ownership intuition. The contracts are called the *Obex* Liquidity Layer, funded through Obex's allocator vault and operated by Obex's people — but the root of the permission tree belongs to Sky. Obex holds delegated operating roles beneath an admin it does not control.

The consequence is that every genuinely structural change to the Liquidity Layer requires Sky, not Obex. Setting rate limit data, setting mint recipients for destination domains, setting LayerZero recipients, and setting maximum slippage are all admin functions (A.6.1.1.5.2.6.1.2.2.1.2.1.1 and A.6.1.1.5.2.6.1.2.2.1.3.2). Obex can move capital within limits; only Sky can change the limits.

That division is the actual security model. Agent-level governance — the 1%-to-propose, 5%-to-pass Root Edit process — never touches these permissions, so a captured Agent electorate cannot widen its own allocation authority. It also means the Agent's autonomy is real but bounded at exactly the boundary Sky cares about: the size and destinations of capital flows, not the day-to-day decisions inside them.
